pending_qa.q: What caused Robinhood to restrict trading during the GameStop saga and was it Robinhood's fault?
pending_qa.r: The GameStop situation wasn't entirely Robinhood's fault because Robinhood has to follow the rules of its clearinghouse, which is Citadel. Citadel told Robinhood to stop trading. The real issue was that Citadel, the clearinghouse run by Ken Griffin, had close connections with a hedge fund that was short GameStop and got caught off-side when Wall Street Bets attacked the short position. Citadel had to restrict buying to manage the lopsided trade.

pending_qa.q: How does the clearinghouse system work and what role does it play in stock trading?
pending_qa.r: When you buy shares on Vanguard, Goldman Sachs, or Robinhood, you believe you own them, but it works like fractional reserve banking. These firms lend out the shares and use them for selling calls, puts, and other derivatives. The clearinghouse, such as Citadel, maintains relationships with multiple brokers and hedge funds. Like a bank keeping $10,000 in reserve on a $100,000 deposit and investing the remaining $90,000 five times over in mortgages, brokerages operate on the same principle with borrowed shares.

pending_qa.q: What risks do amateur investors face when trading options and how does Robinhood educate them?
pending_qa.r: Robinhood requires users to go through a brief questionnaire and education course before trading options, though it is easy to click through most of it. Robinhood provides tools like sliders showing profit and loss scenarios if a stock moves up or down by specific percentages. However, the freedom to access risky investments like options without full understanding can lead to significant losses. Learning by doing is necessary, though most gains typically come after two to three years of experience.

pending_qa.q: Why is Robinhood better positioned than traditional financial institutions to compete in the future of finance?
pending_qa.r: Robinhood is not competing with Goldman Sachs and J.P. Morgan for engineering talent; instead, they compete with OpenAI, Microsoft, and Google in Silicon Valley. This allows them to build cutting-edge technology faster. Robinhood has been building and testing for five to eight years, positioning themselves to lap traditional institutions. They are targeting a new generation of younger investors who are willing to take risks and build wealth, aiming to become the app of the future as this generation matures.

pending_qa.q: How have major financial institutions like JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs changed their stance on blockchain and cryptocurrency?
pending_qa.r: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon says he doesn't like Bitcoin, but JPMorgan likes blockchain and is building on it. Goldman Sachs is also building on blockchain. Over the last two and a half to three years, the shift has been dramatic with Bitcoin ETFs launching and institutional adoption increasing. Even though traditional finance initially rejected crypto as bad, they are now building on blockchain technology because it is not going away.
